To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L-ascorbate acid and D-glucose are effective to reduce GO and restore its electrical conductivity, and the obtained RGOs can be well dispersed in water.
L-AA, D-GLC, and TP are effective green reducing agents for the reduction of graphene oxide and the electrical conductivity of RGO can be enhanced by the existence of ammonia during reduction.

three green reductant, L-AA, D-GLC and TP, are effective to remove oxygen functional groups in GO, and the RGO with L-AA as a reductants and reduced with the assistance of ammonia has the highest electrical conductivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of green reductant for graphene oxide reduction and provides a new way for the preparation of reduced graphene oxide.

the development of green reductant for the production of reduced graphene oxides and provides a new approach to prepare reduced graphene oxide with good electrical conductivity and good dispersibility in aqueous solution.
the green synthesis of graphene materials with the consideration of human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L-AA is a good green reductant and can be applied for the production of RGO.
the green reductants are effective to remove oxygen functional groups in GO, restore the electrical conductivity and enhance the dispersibility of RGO in the aqueous solution.
all the three green reductant are effective in reducing the oxygen-containing groups and restoring the electrical conductivity of RGO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the green reductants could be used as alternatives for chemical reduction of GO, and the reduced graphene oxides obtained with green reductants have great potential to be applied in the preparation of graphene-based composites and conductive ink.
the green reductants are promising in preparing reduced graphene oxide and the obtained RGO with high electrical conductivity is a promising candidate in preparing conductive ink.

the green reductants are effective to reduce GO to graphene materials with high electrical conductivity, and the RGO prepared by L-ascorbics acid as a reductor is the most promising for the preparation of water-dispersible graphene materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the green reductants are efficient for the reduction of GO.
the green reductants can replace the conventional reductants in the preparation of reduced graphene oxides.
the reduced graphene oxide with high electrical conductivity can be produced with green reductants.
